scenes.title: Cash pressure is a timing problem
scenes.text: Payroll is approaching. A customer may pay late. A supplier still needs payment. For a small business, those dates can create a cash gap. Probaho helps the owner see that gap, compare realistic options, and stay in control of the next action.

scenes.title: Meet Probaho
scenes.text: Probaho is an SME finance copilot for Topic E. This presentation uses synthetic Bangladeshi taka records in a local sandbox. The workflow is records, projection, comparison, human approval, execution, and evidence.

scenes.title: A concrete cash gap
scenes.text: Shapla Services starts with one hundred twenty thousand taka. Payroll needs eighty thousand, the supplier bill needs seventy thousand, and a confirmed receivable brings twenty thousand. By October thirty-first, closing cash is minus ten thousand. Against a twenty-thousand reserve floor, the shortfall is thirty thousand.

scenes.title: Records with clear scope
scenes.text: The Records page brings transactions, invoices, and bills together. The owner selects one business and imports a combined CSV. Every row is validated before anything is written. Dates, amounts, currency, and conflicting identifiers are checked, and source records remain linked to the calculations.

scenes.title: What if the customer pays late?
scenes.text: The overview compares scheduled cash with a seven-day late-collection scenario. Here, the receivable falls beyond the target date, so closing cash drops to minus thirty thousand and the reserve gap grows to fifty thousand. The arithmetic uses integer paisa, rather than a language model's estimate.

scenes.title: Compare recovery options
scenes.text: Probaho compares a collection reminder, supplier rescheduling, and mock financing. A reminder creates a draft; it never counts as collected cash. Financing shows illustrative fees and repayment terms, but cannot execute. The supplier option proposes deferring forty thousand taka to November seventh, while protecting payroll.

scenes.title: Human review is a separate step
scenes.text: Before approval, the owner reviews the payee, source bill, amount, dates, assumptions, and policy limits. Approval is a separate human action. Supplier rescheduling also needs a separate acceptance simulation. That button represents a sandbox scenario, not a genuine supplier response.

scenes.title: Execute once and read it back
scenes.text: After both gates, execution changes only the synthetic payment schedule. Target-date closing cash becomes thirty thousand taka, with no reserve shortfall. The deferred supplier obligation still exists. A receipt shows the approved action and before-and-after state. Retrying with the same idempotency key returns the original receipt, instead of executing twice.

scenes.title: Evidence and bounded authority
scenes.text: Plans are bound to the selected business, policy, source records, and sandbox snapshot. Changed details invalidate a pending action. Activity exports include permission events and a per-business hash chain. The assistant has no approval, execution, payment, shell, or SQL tool.
